text:
COST QUALIFICATION, measured after this bead was filed. Detail on bd-01KZYJXC0NNX4HJ1QJ9BDJKPVZ.

I argued here that letting the fixed-query verbs accept a relation and route query-first is SAFE, because introduction.Rmd:331-333 asserts the query-first and materialized values agree to 1e-12, so the plan/materialize distinction concerns what an object retains rather than the answer. That reasoning is correct about values and INCOMPLETE ABOUT COST.

Measured, 216 voxels / 216 searchlights / 6 partition pairs:

  materialized geometry          crossnobis plan (query-first)
    build      0.731 s             build      0.470 s
    contrast   0.151 s             query #1   1.145 s
    contrast   0.027 s             query #2   0.929 s
    rdm        0.026 s             query #3   1.087 s

Geometry amortizes - subsequent questions cost about 3 percent of the build. The query-first path does not amortize at all; every question re-pays in full.

So a user writing three of the proposed one-liners against the same data pays the streaming cost three times, where the materializing path pays once and then answers twice nearly free. The unified verb hides a large economic difference behind identical-looking calls.

This does NOT reverse the recommendation. 1.6x for the learned metric is not a barrier, the ergonomic win is large, and no semantic guarantee is touched. It adds a constraint:

  document the one-liner as the SINGLE-QUESTION form
  show the materialized form as the answer for several questions on the same data
  have the returned view state which path was taken, so a user asking three questions can
  see they paid three times rather than discovering it from wall-clock

Recording this against my own argument rather than quietly amending it, because the earlier reasoning on this bead is what justified calling the wrapper safe.
